_shape: Mirrors the caniuse data model. Agents (their browsers) carry a version_list with an era index and a release date, and capability files carry stats as a version to support-code map. Era 0 is the release we measured, negative is older, positive is newer. Versions with no entry in a capability's stats render as not yet measured.

stable.label: Defined in the released MCP specification

draft.label: Defined only in a draft revision of the MCP specification

proposed.label: Proposed, not yet in any published specification

deprecated.label: Defined in the released MCP specification but deprecated in this revision, and eligible for removal no earlier than the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28

extension.label: Defined in an official opt-in extension rather than the core specification, and disabled unless both sides negotiate it

support_codes.y: exposed to the agent at the declared capture boundary
support_codes.a: changed at the boundary or reachable only elsewhere
support_codes.x: the adapter cannot negotiate this protocol revision, so no capability is reachable

defaults.inclusion_rule: A framework is listed if it ships a first-party or officially documented MCP adapter. Nothing is excluded on quality grounds.
defaults.order_rule: Alphabetical within language group. No ranking is implied or computed.
defaults.version_policy: Era 0 is the framework release tested for this protocol snapshot. An unmeasured cell means no same-protocol adapter capture was produced.
defaults.green_rule: Every cell answers one question: does this framework expose this MCP capability to the agent at its declared capture boundary? For a value carried in a tool definition, 'y' means the value is present there unchanged. For a protocol feature, 'y' means the adapter gives the agent a working path to it and a scan exercised that path. A capability the framework could support but does not is not 'y'.
defaults.partial_rule: 'a' means the capability is reachable but not on the terms the specification sets: the note must say whether the value was transformed at the boundary, only partly preserved, retained somewhere the agent does not read, or supported only for part of the feature.
defaults.surface_rule: surface.json enumerates what MCP 2026-07-28 defines, and it is maintained separately from what we have measured. Any feature in it without a capability file is published with every cell 'u'. Coverage is therefore computed from the two files rather than asserted, and a feature cannot be quietly dropped from the denominator to make coverage look better.
defaults.note_rule: Every 'a' and 'n' cell must carry a #n note reference naming the exact mechanism, so a status can be checked rather than trusted.
defaults.usage_rule: No adoption weighting is published. We have no defensible source yet, and an invented percentage would be the least trustworthy number on the page.

crewai.name: CrewAI

capture_boundary.capture_object: CrewAI BaseTool name, description, and args_schema
capture_boundary.protocol_version_evidence: Dependency resolution rejects mcp 2.0.0 before the adapter can run.

result_boundaries.label: Agent tool invocation
result_boundaries.capture_object: the value ToolUsage hands back during a crew run
result_boundaries.limitation: CrewStructuredTool.invoke is driven directly. No LLM was bound and no crew was kicked off.

crewai.measurement_note: CrewAI 1.15.1 requires MCP Python SDK 1.26.x, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.

langchain.name: LangChain

capture_boundary.protocol_version_evidence: Dependency resolution rejects mcp 2.0.0 before the adapter can run.

result_boundaries.label: Direct tool invocation
result_boundaries.capture_object: the tool return value, before any ToolMessage is built

result_boundaries.label: Agent tool invocation
result_boundaries.capture_object: the ToolMessage an agent or ToolNode puts in the message list
result_boundaries.limitation: The ToolMessage is built by langchain_core from the same call a ToolNode makes. No chat model was bound and no provider request was captured.

langchain.measurement_note: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 requires mcp<2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.

openai-agents.name: OpenAI Agents SDK

capture_boundary.protocol_version_evidence: protocol version exposed by the MCPServer client session

result_boundaries.label: Agent tool invocation
result_boundaries.capture_object: the ToolOutput the agent loop feeds back to the model
result_boundaries.limitation: The FunctionTool callable is driven directly. No model implementation was bound and no provider request was captured.

openai-agents.measurement_note: Measured through the real OpenAI Agents SDK adapter.

pydantic-ai.name: Pydantic AI

result_boundaries.label: Direct toolset call
result_boundaries.capture_object: the mapped toolset result, or the exception it raises

result_boundaries.label: Agent toolset call
result_boundaries.capture_object: the value the agent's tool executor receives
result_boundaries.limitation: The toolset method is driven directly. The agent's own conversion of a raised ModelRetry into a RetryPromptPart happens above this boundary and is not captured here.

pydantic-ai.measurement_note: Measured through the real Pydantic AI MCPToolset adapter.

mastra.name: Mastra

capture_boundary.capture_object: Mastra Tool action returned by listTools
capture_boundary.protocol_version_evidence: protocolVersion observed from the pinned @modelcontextprotocol/sdk client used by MCPClient.listTools

result_boundaries.label: Agent tool invocation, onToolError: 'throw' (default)
result_boundaries.capture_object: the tool action return value, or the MastraError it throws
result_boundaries.limitation: The tool action is executed directly. No AI SDK provider was bound and no provider request was captured.

result_boundaries.label: Agent tool invocation, onToolError: 'return'
result_boundaries.capture_api: @mastra/mcp tool action execute, server configured onToolError: 'return'
result_boundaries.capture_object: the CallToolResult envelope the action resolves with
result_boundaries.limitation: This is a documented non-default server option, not the behaviour a caller gets without configuring it.

mastra.measurement_note: Mastra 1.17.3 negotiated MCP 2025-11-25. The scanner refused to compare that capture with a 2026-07-28 source.
